candidate_relations.reason: Fever and tachycardia can indicate abdominal sepsis as a state, not Burkitt lymphoma.
GIST is an adult mesenchymal tumor, not the typical cause of pediatric small-bowel intussusception with Hb 4 g/dL.
IgA vasculitis can cause intussusception in children but does not produce this large RUQ mass and profound anemia as Burkitt does.
Lymphoma is the correct family but omits Burkitt subtype.
Meckel diverticulum can lead to intussusception but does not explain a 4×5 cm mass with Hb 4 g/dL.
Gastrointestinal bleeding is inferred from pallor and Hb 4 g/dL, a manifestation of the tumor, not the lymphoma type.
Inflammatory bowel disease is not the mass-forming intussusception diagnosis.
Infectious enteritis does not produce a palpable 4×5 cm mass.
Hematological disorder is a vague parent of lymphoma/anemia.
Gastroenteritis does not explain intussusception plus a visible abdominal mass.
Intestinal lymphoma is the anatomic parent missing Burkitt specificity.
Imaging-diagnosed small-bowel intussusception is the presenting mechanism, not the underlying Burkitt lymphoma.
Hemorrhagic shock physiology from Hb 4 g/dL is a consequence, not the tumor diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Adolescent ileocolic intussusception with a right-upper-quadrant mass and severe anemia is a classic Burkitt presentation; no candidate names Burkitt lymphoma.
